headline: A 2008 executive order by President Bush aimed at limiting federal spending on earmarks, which are funds set aside by Congress for specific projects.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order directs the executive branch to limit spending on congressional earmarks it considers wasteful. Earmarks are funds that lawmakers direct to specific local projects or recipients. No summary was provided, so the exact rules and limits are not described here.

who_it_affects.how: They would likely face new limits on how they handle and spend money tied to earmarks.

who_it_affects.group: Organizations and local governments that receive earmarked funds
who_it_affects.how: They could see changes in whether they receive money that Congress directed to their projects.

when_it_takes_effect: Likely on signing, January 29, 2008 (not confirmed by the source material).
